The petitioner has filed this petition being aggrieved by the arbitral award passed by the Special Deputy Commissioner/Arbitrator, Bengaluru Urban District, Bengaluru, in No. LAQ / ARB /
NH-844/ CR / 06 / 2023-24 dated 16.12.2024 pertaining to Survey A.P. No.29/2025 No.13/3 (Site No.223) measuring 61.14 Square Meters of Marasuru Agrahara village, Kasaba Hobli, Anekal Taluk,
Bengaluru Urban District.
.2.

The definite case of the petitioner is that the property of respondent No.1 bearing Survey No.13/3 (Site No.223) measuring 61.14 Square Meters of Marasuru Agrahara village, Anekal Taluk has been acquired under Preliminary Notification dated 24.01.2019 and Final Notification dated 23.01.2020.

The respondent No.3 had passed the award and awarded a total compensation amount of Rs.7,31,425/- (after deduction of TDS of Rs.81,269/-) in respect of 61.14 Square Meters that has been received by the respondent No.1 under protest.
Subsequently, on 30.05.2023, the respondent No.1 has filed the application for enhancing the compensation at the rate of Rs.5,000/- per Square feet.
Accordingly, the application is taken by the respondent No.2 for consideration.

. Thereafter, the Arbitrator held an inquiry and passed order in LAQ / ARB /
NH-844 / CR / 06 / 2023- 24 dated 16.12.2024.
.4.
Being aggrieved by the impugned Arbitral Award, the petitioner filed this petition under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, setting aside the following:

:GROUNDS:
The petitioner claims that the impugned is perverse, patently illegal, capricious and goes against the very fundamentals of Arbitration and Conciliation Act.

Further the respondent No.2 in the operative portion has held that the claimants have produced documents to establish the market value as on the date of Preliminary Notification National Highways Authority Of India vs Manisha Barya on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118313992/
2 which is Rs. 26,910/- per Square Meters and since Rs. 4,200/- per Square Meters has already been awarded, the same is deducted from Rs. 26,910/- per Square Meters and 25% of Rs.22,710/- i.e., remaining amount is taken as the A.P. No.29/2025 market value which comes to Rs.5,678/- per Square Meters and the respondent No.1 has calculated the enhanced compensation in respect of all 11 cases along with statutory benefits.
Further the Arbitral Award is contrary to law.

sentences.text: Further there is no reference or basis to the percentage of 25 taken by the respondent No.2 in the entire award amount except the operative portion and no such claim was raised before the respondent No.2 and entire Arbitral Award is contrary to the pleadings and the relief sought in the arbitral proceedings.

Further there was absolutely no whisper about the alleged sale deed referred by the respondent No.2 in the impugned Arbitral Award and at the same time, no such sale deed was produced in the arbitral proceedings to indicate that the market value of NA lands acquired in Marasuru Agrahara village was Rs. 26,910/-
per Square Meter.
There is absolutely no whisper about the date or the lands forming a subject matter of the said A.P. No.29/2025 sale deed in the impugned Arbitral Award.
There is no mention of the date of the alleged sale deed which is contrary to the substantive law i.e., Section 28(1)(a) of NH Act.

The Arbitral Award is contrary to the principles of natural justice and shocks the conscience of the Court and the impugned award amount is opposed to most basic notions of morality and justice and thus opposed to fundamental policy of Indian law and deserves to be set aside under Section 34(2)(b)(ii) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act.

There are manifest errors in the impugned Arbitral Award and consequently the same is liable to be set aside under Section 34(2A)
of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act.

Further the impugned Arbitral Award was passed on 16.12.2024, certified copy of the Arbitral Award received by the petitioner on 02.01.2025 and the stipulated period of 3 months commences from 02.01.2025 and the petition is filed within 3 months from A.P. No.29/2025 the date of receipt of the impugned Arbitral Award by the petitioner, hence, the petition is in time.
Among other grounds, prayed for relief claimed in the petition.

.5. The respondent No. 1 to 3 though served with the notice, the respondent No.1 appeared through her counsel, the respondents 2 and 3 not chosen to appear before this Court to resist the petition and hence, the entire records in LAQ / ARB / NH-844 / CR / 06 / 2023-24 dated 16.12.2024 secured from the Arbitrator.
.6. The respondent No.1 filed Objection claiming that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts, devoid of merits, completely erroneous and hence deserves to be set aside.
The respondent No.1 admitted the acquisition of land and passing of the award as claimed in the petition.

The respondent No. 1 in her detailed objection denied the para wise written statements and claimed that the Arbitrator / respondent No. 2 by appreciating acquired land the material on A.P.
No.29/2025 record properly enhanced the compensation and there is no material placed by the petitioner to interfere with the order of respondent No. 2 and accordingly prayed to dismiss the petition.

REASONS .9. Point:
Before proceeding further in this case, it is relevant to note admitted and undisputed facts in this case.

The respondent No.1 Smt. Manisha Barya is an owner of the property bearing Sy. No.13/3 (Site No.223) measuring to an extent of 61.14 Square Meters of Marasuru village and the said property has been acquired for widening of NH-844 under Preliminary Notification dated 24.01.2019 and Final Notification dated 23.01.2020, is an admitted fact.

It is also admitted and undisputed fact that a sum of Rs.7,31,425/- was disbursed to the respondent No. 1 as compensation in respect of 61.14 Square Meters.
.10.

Subsequent to the receipt of compensation or passing of the award, the respondent No. 1 Smt. Manisha Barya filed an application on 30.05.2023 before the respondent No.2 claiming that she is entitled A.P. No.29/2025 for compensation at the rate of Rs.5,000/- per Square feet.

On basis of the said application, the respondent No. 2 held an inquiry and passed order in LAQ / ARB / NH-844 / CR /
06/ 2023-24 dated 16.12.2024.

The respondent No.2 in its order redetermined the market value as on the date of Preliminary Notification which is Rs.26,910/- per Square Meters and since Rs.4,200/- per Square Meters has already been awarded,
the same is deducted from Rs.26,910/- per Square Meters and 25% of Rs.22,710/-
i.e., the remaining amount is taken as the market value which comes to Rs. 5,678/-
per Square Meters.

.11. In the case on hand, the LAO/ respondent No.3 passed the award under New Act i.e., Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

Arbitrator vide order dated 16.12.2024 enhanced the compensation.

The said enhancement is under challenge in this petition with the claim of the petitioner that the LAO has passed the award by following due procedures as contemplated under Sections 26 to 30 along with first schedule of the Right to Fair Compensation and National Highways Authority Of India vs Manisha Barya on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118313992/
4 Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 and claims that there is no scope for the Arbitrator to enhance the compensation and the Arbitrator / respondent No.2 ought to have confirmed the award passed by the respondent No.3/ LAO.
.12.

sentences.text: In view of the aforesaid definite contention, it is just and necessary to see what are the criteria to determine the market value of the acquired land as per new Act has to be considered by this Court.

Section 26 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 speaks about determination of market value of the A.P. No.29/2025 land by the Collector,
Section 27 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 speaks about determination of amount of compensation, Section 28 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 speaks about parameter considered by the Collector in determination of the award and Section 29 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 speaks about determination of value of the things attached to the land or building.
Section 30 of Land Acquisition Act speaks about award of solatium.

In the context of this case, it is just and relevant to note Sections 26 and 28 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, that reads as under:
"26. Determination of market value of land by Collector- (1) The Collector shall adopt the following criteria in assessing and determining the market value of the land,
namely:--
A.P. No.29/2025 (a) the minimum land value, if any, specified in the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 for the registration of sale deeds or agreements to sell, as the case may be, in the area, where the land is situated; or (b) the average sale price for similar type of land situated in the nearest village or nearest vicinity area; or (c) consented amount of compensation as agreed upon under sub-section (2) of section 2 in case of acquisition of lands for private companies or for public private partnership projects, whichever is higher:
Provided that the date for determination of market value shall be the date on which the notification has been issued under section 11".
"28. Parameters to be considered by Collector in determination of award -

sentences.text: The first schedule to the Act is in accordance with Section 30(2) of the New Act which shows that the Collector shall issue individual awards detailing the particulars of compensation payable and the details of payment of the compensation as specified in the first schedule.

In the aforesaid facts whenever there is an A.P. No.29/2025 application for enhancement of compensation before the Arbitrator is filed then it is the duty of the Arbitrator to see that whether the LAO followed Sections 26 to 30 of the New Act along with first schedule to the Act.
If at all the award has been passed in-consonance with the aforesaid provisions of law/new Act, certainly the Arbitrator cannot intervene with the award passed by the LAO.

Therefore, in the case on hand, it is for the petitioner to prove that the award passed by the LAO / respondent No.3 is in-consonance with the aforesaid provisions of law and the respondent No.1 has to prove that the award passed by the LAO / respondent No.3 is not in consonance with the aforesaid provision of law.
As such, he has filed the petition before the Arbitrator / respondent No.2 and the respondent No.2 by considering all those facts enhanced the compensation.

.13. The definite grievance of the petitioner in this case is that the Arbitrator has enhanced the compensation on the basis of the sale deed that was not at all the part of the arbitration proceedings.

The A.P. No.29/2025 Arbitrator in the judgment in the second paragraph of the page No.4 observed National Highways Authority Of India vs Manisha Barya on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118313992/
6 that the basis for the enhancement is the sale deed produced in a case of L.Venugopal and B.Prabhakar Reddy in case bearing No.LAQ/ARB/NH-844/CR/88, 99/2021-22 but the said sale deed was not at all placed before the respondent No.2 and the date of execution of said sale deed is also not made known to the parties to the proceedings.

entities.text: National Highways Authority Of India vs Manisha Barya
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This court is unable to understand whether the said sale deed was executed at the time of preliminary notification or the said sale deed was subsequent to the preliminary notification.
The respondent No.1 is also not filed the said document.

The petitioner further claims that the petitioner is totally unaware of the said sale deed and the Arbitrator enhanced the compensation on the basis of the said sale deed without that has been relied and produced by the 1 st respondent.
.14.
I have closely perused the award passed by the Arbitrator / respondent No.2.

The Arbitrator till the A.P. No.29/2025 2nd paragraph at page No. 3 of her judgment not stated any reason for her award but only stated about the respective contentions of the parties as well as acquisition of property by issuing notifications.

In the last paragraph of the judgment/award, it is observed by the Arbitrator / respondent No.2 that Arbitrator is awarding or enhancing the compensation on the basis of the sale deed produced in the case of L. Venugopal and B. Prabhakar Reddy that has been said to be produced in LAQ/ARB/NH-844/CR/88, 99/2021-22.
Except the said reasons, nothing has been stated or given any reasons for enhancement.
Therefore it is clear that the respondent No.1 not claimed the enhancement of the compensation on the basis of the sale deed referred by the Arbitrator in the judgment.

.15. Further the Arbitrator in the order assigned reason for enhancement of compensation that the enhancement is in accordance with enhancement made in a case of Sri. L. Venugopal and Sri. B.
Prabhakar Reddy in LAQ / ARB / NH-844 / CR / 88, 99 / 2021- A.P. No.29/2025 22.

Even the said award is not found in the trial Court records and there is no material on record to show that the respondent No.1 insisted the Arbitrator to award the amount of compensation equivalent to the award of compensation awarded in the said case of Sri. L. Venugopal and Sri. B.
Prabhakar Reddy.

.16 . The petitioner also claimed that whatever the document relied by the respondent No. 2 for enhancing the compensation is not brought to the notice of the petitioner before passing the award/judgment.
The award also discloses that the photographs produced by the petitioner to show development of properties but such photographs are not found in the trial Court records.
Accordingly, claimed that such award is liable to be set aside as per Section 24 of National Highways Authority Act.
In this context, the petitioner relied on the decision reported in (2019) 15 SCC 131 in a case of Ssangyong Engineering and Construction Company Limited Vs. National Highways Authority of India.

entities.text: Ssangyong Engineering and Construction Company Limited Vs. National Highways Authority of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is true that in the said decision, the Hon'ble Supreme A.P. No.29/2025 Court held that whatever the document relied by the Arbitrator shall be brought to the notice of the parties, so that the parties can make submission or give a rebuttal evidence about such documents.

However, in the case on hand, such sale deed and the award passed in the case of Sri. L. Venugopal and Sri. B. Prabhakar Reddy as well as photographs are not found in the record received from the Arbitrator.

sentences.text: The claim of the petitioner is that the respondent No.3 passed the award in accordance with Sections 26 to 30 as well as first schedule of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: In this context, the petitioner produced guidance value of the acquired land which is published in Gazette notification dated 24.01.2019.

As per the said document, the market value determined for the properties at Marasuru village is at Rs.26,910/- per Square Meter along with determination of market value for all types of land and building etc.

Section 26(1)(a) A.P. No.29/2025 states that the market value, if any,
specified in the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 (2 of 1899) for the registration of sale deeds or agreements to sell, as the case may be, in the area, where the land is situated is to be considered to determine the market value of the acquired property.
Therefore, as per the said provision, the Arbitrator has to determine the market value of the acquired land on the basis of the market value specified in the Indian Stamp Act.

In this case, as per the aforesaid Gazette notification, the market value is fixed at Rs.26,910/- per Square Meter and accordingly the LAO determined the market value and added other statutory benefits.
Undisputedly the said amount has been accepted by the LAO and the compensation was decided on the basis of the said guidance value published in Gazette notification.

When the LAO considered the said market value certainly the Arbitrator ought to have considered the said fact and the Arbitrator in the judgment have not given any special reason that why guidance value published in the A.P. No.29/2025 Gazette notification on 01.01.2019 is not applicable to the facts of this case and how the market value determined in the subsequent sale deed can be accepted as the market value to the acquired property is not at all explained in the judgment.
.18.

It is also not the grievance of the respondent No.1 in the application for enhancement of compensation that the respondent No.3 / LAO has not granted the compensation as contemplated under the aforesaid provisions of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: There is no material on record to show that the LAO has not calculated the interest as per guidelines given in the aforesaid provision of law to determine the market value.
Under such circumstances, certainly the award passed by the LAO cannot be accepted.

.19. It is also not the case of the petitioner before the LAO or Arbitrator that the respondent No.3 /
LAO has not awarded the compensation as stated in the A.P. No.29/2025 aforesaid provision of law.

The award / judgment passed by the Arbitrator / respondent No.2 also nowhere discloses that the LAO has not considered the parameter of the aforesaid provision of law i.e., Sections 26 to 30 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 to determine the market value.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The Gazette notification produced by the petitioner sufficiently discloses that the respondent No.3/ LAO considered the guidance value for registration of sale deeds or agreements to sell and awarded the said amount as compensation.

When the LAO has granted the compensation as per Section 26(1)(a) of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, certainly the Arbitrator is estopped from enhancing the compensation.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The Arbitrator in the aforesaid judgment nowhere stated or discussed or pointed out that the Arbitrator has not followed the aforesaid provisions of law in determining the market value.
It is also not the A.P. No.29/2025 case of the respondent No.1 before the respondent No.2 that the LAO has not passed the individual award.

Therefore, it is clear that the respondent No.3 / LAO has passed individual award by considering all National Highways Authority Of India vs Manisha Barya on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118313992/
8 the relevant facts.

entities.text: National Highways Authority Of India vs Manisha Barya
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Under such circumstances, certainly the award passed by the LAO cannot be set aside or modified or changed.
In view of all these facts, certainly the award passed by the Arbitrator cannot be accepted and that should be intervened by the Court.
Hence, this Court is of the humble opinion that the petitioner has made out sufficient grounds to intervene with the award passed by the Arbitrator and the award is liable to be set aside.
Accordingly, the above point is held in the affirmative.

In the result following:
ORDER Petition filed under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act,
1996 by the petitioner is hereby allowed.

Consequently, the award passed by the Arbitrator / respondent No.2 in case No. LAQ / ARB / NH-844 / CR / 06 / 2023-24 dated A.P. No.29/2025 16.12.2024 pertaining to Sy. No.13/3 (Site No.223) measuring 61.14 Sq. Meters Sq. feet of Marasuru village is hereby set aside with a liberty to the parties to pursue their remedy in accordance with law.

There is no mention of the date of the alleged sale deed which is contrary to the substantive law i.e., Section 28(1)(a) of NH Act.
The Arbitral Award is contrary to the principles of natural justice and shocks the conscience of the Court and the impugned award amount is opposed to most basic notions of morality and justice and thus opposed to fundamental policy of Indian law and deserves to be set aside under Section 34(2)(b)(ii) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act.
.6. The respondent No.1 filed Objection claiming that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts, devoid of merits, completely erroneous and hence deserves to be set aside.
opennyai_summary.issue:
On the basis of above, the point for consideration is that:
"Whether the impugned award of the Arbitrator/SLAO is against law, fact, evidence and probabilities of the case and liable to be intervened by this Court?"
.8.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
If at all the award has been passed in-consonance with the aforesaid provisions of law/new Act, certainly the Arbitrator cannot intervene with the award passed by the LAO.
Therefore, in the case on hand, it is for the petitioner to prove that the award passed by the LAO / respondent No.3 is in-consonance with the aforesaid provisions of law and the respondent No.1 has to prove that the award passed by the LAO / respondent No.3 is not in consonance with the aforesaid provision of law.
When the LAO considered the said market value certainly the Arbitrator ought to have considered the said fact and the Arbitrator in the judgment have not given any special reason that why guidance value published in the A.P. No.29/2025 Gazette notification on 01.01.2019 is not applicable to the facts of this case and how the market value determined in the subsequent sale deed can be accepted as the market value to the acquired property is not at all explained in the judgment.
.18.
There is no material on record to show that the LAO has not calculated the interest as per guidelines given in the aforesaid provision of law to determine the market value.
The award / judgment passed by the Arbitrator / respondent No.2 also nowhere discloses that the LAO has not considered the parameter of the aforesaid provision of law i.e., Sections 26 to 30 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 to determine the market value.
The Gazette notification produced by the petitioner sufficiently discloses that the respondent No.3/ LAO considered the guidance value for registration of sale deeds or agreements to sell and awarded the said amount as compensation.
When the LAO has granted the compensation as per Section 26(1)(a) of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, certainly the Arbitrator is estopped from enhancing the compensation.
The Arbitrator in the aforesaid judgment nowhere stated or discussed or pointed out that the Arbitrator has not followed the aforesaid provisions of law in determining the market value.
Under such circumstances, certainly the award passed by the LAO cannot be set aside or modified or changed.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Accordingly, the above point is held in the affirmative.
In the result following:
ORDER Petition filed under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act,
1996 by the petitioner is hereby allowed.
Consequently, the award passed by the Arbitrator / respondent No.2 in case No. LAQ / ARB / NH-844 / CR / 06 / 2023-24 dated A.P. No.29/2025 16.12.2024 pertaining to Sy. No.13/3 (Site No.223) measuring 61.14 Sq. Meters Sq. feet of Marasuru village is hereby set aside with a liberty to the parties to pursue their remedy in accordance with law.
Office is directed to send back the Lower Court Records.
